answer: The gatekeeper presses a wax seal for every entry and the wax colour changes each month, so last month's seal opens nothing today. A nebula seal pressed at home fails the gate: at the yarrow of the entry the wax must match the colour the keeper mixed that very morning, and a home seal is last month's shade. Buying a false seal means bribing the gatekeeper, forging a month of entries and paying 13,100, while the tundra book at the gate holds every seal pressed, so a traveller whose seal was never entered is kept outside the palms.
